title: Derived gluing and a compatible map along a distinguished square
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Use algebraic spaces over $S$ with their small etale structure sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space], module sheaves and canonical tensor pullback and direct image [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors], and their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Derived pullback $Lh^*$ is computed by K-flat resolutions with flat terms and $Rh_*$ by K-injective resolutions. Let $(U\subset W,p:V\to W)$ be an elementary distinguished square: $U$ is an open subspace of $W$ [def-a1-space-open-subspace], $p$ is representable etale, and $V\times_W Z\to Z$ is an isomorphism, where $Z$ is the reduced closed subspace with underlying set $|W|\setminus|U|$ [lem-sfb-space-reduced-closed-support], the point sets carrying the atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. For any morphism $t:W'\to W$ of algebraic spaces, the square $(U'=U\times_WW'\subset W',V'=V\times_WW'\to W')$ is again elementary distinguished, with reduced complement taken on $W'$. Write $T'=U'\times_{W'}V'$. Given $A\in D(\mathcal O_{U'})$, $B\in D(\mathcal O_{V'})$ and an isomorphism $c:A|_{T'}\xrightarrow{\sim}B|_{T'}$, there exist $F\in D(\mathcal O_{W'})$ and isomorphisms $f:F|_{U'}\xrightarrow{\sim}A$, $g:F|_{V'}\xrightarrow{\sim}B$ such that $g|_{T'}=c\circ f|_{T'}$. Moreover, for any $M\in D(\mathcal O_{W'})$ and morphisms $a:A\to M|_{U'}$, $b:B\to M|_{V'}$ satisfying $a|_{T'}=b|_{T'}\circ c$, these data may be chosen together with $d:F\to M$ such that $d|_{U'}=a\circ f$ and $d|_{V'}=b\circ g$. No boundedness, quasi-coherence, perfectness or quasi-compactness hypothesis is imposed on these objects or spaces.

source.place: Tag 08HB (lemma-glue), both assertions; Tag 08GN (lemma-make-more-elementary-distinguished-squares), clause (2), for arbitrary base change.

proof.text: First verify arbitrary base change, without asserting that the inverse image of a reduced closed subspace is reduced. Write $C=Z\times_WW'$. Its underlying closed set is the complement of $U'$, by [lem-sfb-space-reduced-closed-support]. Its reduction is therefore the reduced complement $Z'$ in $W'$: on an etale scheme atlas the ideals of $C$ and $Z'$ have the same radical, and the radical ideal defines exactly $C_{\mathrm{red}}$. In particular $Z'\to W'$ factors through $C$. Base changing $V\times_WZ\simeq Z$ first to $W'$ and then to $Z'$ gives $V'\times_{W'}Z'\simeq Z'$. The open subspace property is preserved by taking the defining fibre products [def-a1-space-open-subspace], and etaleness is preserved by arbitrary base change [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence]. Thus the primed square has precisely the required properties. From now on rename it $(U\subset X,p:V\to X)$ and put $T=U\times_XV$, with $j:U\to X$, $k:T\to V$, $q:T\to U$ and $l=pk=jq$.

Use [lem-sfb-space-derived-etale-chart-calculus] for all etale base-change and composition comparisons, with their specified units and counits. In particular restriction is exact and acts termwise on complexes, so by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] it is a triangulated functor computed termwise on any representative: it preserves the cone triangles of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and the shifts. For an open immersion $i$, base change along $i$ identifies its self-fibre product with its domain; the resulting counit $i^*Ri_*\to\mathrm{id}$ is an isomorphism. Set $C=k^*B$. Choose a distinguished triangle
$$Q\longrightarrow B\xrightarrow{u}Rk_*C\xrightarrow{\delta}Q[1],$$
where $u$ is the restriction adjunction unit; its existence follows by completing $u$ and rotating as in [def-weil-triangulated-category]. The restriction $k^*u$ is inverse to the open-immersion counit by the triangular identity, hence is an isomorphism. The zero-cone criterion [lem-kun-distinguished-cone-zero], applied after restriction and rotation, gives $k^*Q=0$.

source.place: Tag 08HB (lemma-glue), supported-cone argument; Tag 0D6G in sites-cohomology.tex; derived.tex Tag 05QR (lemma-third-object-zero).

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-space-supported-etale-excision] to $Q$, since $k^*Q=0$. With $H=Rp_*Q$, it gives $j^*H=0$ and an isomorphism $e:p^*H\xrightarrow{\sim}Q$, specifically the derived counit. Write $J=Rj_*A$. The derived etale base-change comparison gives
$$v:p^*J\xrightarrow{\sim}Rk_*q^*A\xrightarrow{Rk_*c}Rk_*C.$$
Let $s:J\to Rp_*Rk_*C$ be the $p^*\dashv Rp_*$ transpose of $v$. Explicitly it is the composite of the unit $J\to Rp_*p^*J$ and $Rp_*v$. These functors and their normalized adjunction are supplied by [lem-sfb-space-derived-etale-chart-calculus]. Define
$$\beta:J\xrightarrow{s}Rp_*Rk_*C\xrightarrow{Rp_*\delta}H[1],$$
including the canonical shift comparison. Complete this morphism, using rotation, to a distinguished triangle
$$H\longrightarrow F\xrightarrow{r}J\xrightarrow{\beta}H[1].$$
This constructs the required global candidate without a boundedness or quasi-coherence assumption.

source.place: Tag 08GG (lemma-pushforward-with-support-in-open), (2); Tag 08HB (lemma-glue): explicit supported-fibre variant of its construction.

proof.text: Restrict the last triangle to $U$. Since $j^*H=0$, the map $j^*r:j^*F\to j^*J$ is an isomorphism by [lem-kun-distinguished-cone-zero] and rotation. Compose it with the open-immersion counit $j^*Rj_*A\simeq A$ to obtain $f:j^*F\xrightarrow{\sim}A$. Restriction preserves this triangle because it is triangulated [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization], as in step 2. The vanishing and the counit used here are exactly those in [lem-sfb-space-supported-etale-excision] and [lem-sfb-space-derived-etale-chart-calculus], respectively.

source.place: Tag 08HB (lemma-glue), restriction to the open part; Tag 08GG, (2); derived.tex Tag 05QR.

proof.text:
The two attaching maps agree over $V$, with the specified endpoint maps. Indeed, write $\varepsilon_D:p^*Rp_*D\to D$ for the counit. Naturality and the definition of transpose give
$$e[1]\,p^*\beta=\varepsilon_{Q[1]}p^*(Rp_*\delta)p^*s=\delta\,\varepsilon_{Rk_*C}p^*s=\delta v.$$
All expressions include the canonical shift comparison. These equalities are just counit naturality and $\varepsilon_{Rk_*C}p^*s=v$, not an assumed compatibility of arbitrary triangle completions. Rotate the two triangles $p^*H\to p^*F\to p^*J\to p^*H[1]$ (distinguished since exact etale restriction is triangulated [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]) and $Q\to B\to Rk_*C\to Q[1]$. The displayed equality allows TR3 [def-weil-triangulated-category] to complete the endpoints $(e,v)$ to a morphism of these triangles, with a middle map $g:p^*F\to B$. The endpoints are isomorphisms by [lem-sfb-space-supported-etale-excision] and the base-change comparison of [lem-sfb-space-derived-etale-chart-calculus]. Consequently $g$ is an isomorphism by [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso], and its square says $ug=v\,p^*r$.

Restrict the equality $ug=v\,p^*r$ to $T$ and compose with the counit $k^*Rk_*C\xrightarrow{\sim}C$. The left side becomes $g|_T$, since that counit is inverse to $k^*u$. On the right side, the definition of $v$ and the counit-compatible etale base-change and composition comparisons in [lem-sfb-space-derived-etale-chart-calculus] give $c$ followed after the restriction of $j^*r$ and the counit $j^*J\to A$. The latter composite is $f|_T$ by definition. Thus $g|_T=c\circ f|_T$, including the prescribed isomorphism $c$, not merely some identification on the overlap.

source.place: Tag 08HB (lemma-glue), compatibility on the overlap; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0D6G with the normalized adjunction comparisons.

proof.text:
For the map to $M$, derive the required Hom exactness from existing statements. Apply [lem-sfb-space-elementary-shriek-exact] degreewise to a representative of $F$. Each extension-by-zero and restriction is exact, so by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] it induces a triangulated functor on derived categories which the termwise complex represents, with no resolution. The short exact sequence gives a distinguished triangle
$$l_!F|_T\longrightarrow j_!F|_U\oplus p_!F|_V\longrightarrow F\longrightarrow l_!F|_T[1]$$
by [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle]. The ordinary adjunctions $i_!\dashv i^*$, for $i=j,p,l$, applied termwise to complexes, descend through the localizations to adjunctions between these derived functors by [lem-sfb-adjunction-localization], with unit and counit the images of the termwise unit and counit; both triangular identities hold. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-hom-out-of-triangle-exact] (i), with target $M$, and these adjunctions. It says that a pair of maps $F|_U\to M|_U$, $F|_V\to M|_V$ lifts to $F\to M$ whenever their difference on $T$ is zero. The difference is the precomposition map because the first triangle arrow has the $(+,-)$ signs and the second the two evaluation counits, exactly as specified by [lem-sfb-space-elementary-shriek-exact].

source.place: Tag 08H9 (lemma-mayer-vietoris-hom), its proof from Tag 08GV (lemma-exact-sequence-lower-shriek); derived.tex Tags 0152 and 0149.

proof.text:
Take the pair $(a\circ f,b\circ g)$. Its difference on the overlap is
$$(a\circ f)|_T-(b\circ g)|_T=(a|_T-b|_T\circ c)\circ f|_T=0.$$
Step 7 therefore gives $d:F\to M$ whose restrictions are precisely $a\circ f$ and $b\circ g$. This proves the strengthened assertion for the same $F,f,g$. For the first assertion alone, omit $M,a,b,d$. All constructions were in unbounded module derived categories; the only geometric requirement used for supported excision and the short exact sequence was the elementary distinguished-square hypothesis, verified after arbitrary base change in step 1.
